title: Counit calculus for augmented arrows and arbitrary resolutions
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with homotopy and derived categories and localizations $Q:K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$, $Q':K(\mathcal B)\to D(\mathcal B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix functors $G:K(\mathcal A)\to K(\mathcal B)$ and $L:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$, and a natural transformation $\tau:LQ\to Q'G$. Fix a class $\mathcal P$ on which $\tau$ is invertible. For a category $\mathcal X$, let $S,R:\mathcal X\to K(\mathcal A)$ and $a:S\to R$ be a natural transformation with $S(X)\in\mathcal P$ for every $X$. Set
$$w_X=L(Qa_X)\tau_{S(X)}^{-1}:Q'G(S(X))\to L(QR(X)).$$
For any quasi-isomorphism $r:H\to R(X)$ with $H\in\mathcal P$, the map
$$\chi_r=\tau_H L(Qr)^{-1}:L(QR(X))\xrightarrow{\sim}Q'G(H)$$
is an isomorphism satisfying $Q'G(r)\chi_r=\tau_{R(X)}$ and $Q'G(r)\chi_rw_X=Q'G(a_X)$. For any two such resolutions put $c_{s,r}=\chi_s\chi_r^{-1}$. These maps satisfy $c_{s,r}\chi_rw_X=\chi_sw_X$, $c_{t,s}c_{s,r}=c_{t,r}$ and $c_{r,r}=1$. If $h:H\to H'$ satisfies $sh=r$, then $Q'G(h)=c_{s,r}$; no such $h$ is required to exist. For every $f:X\to Y$, put $B(f)=Q'G(S(f))$ and $D(f)=L(QR(f))$. Then
$$D(f)w_X=w_YB(f).$$
If a class $W$ of arrows of $\mathcal X$ is carried to isomorphisms by both $B$ and $D$, these maps descend as a natural transformation on $\mathcal X[W^{-1}]$; explicitly $w_XB(f)^{-1}=D(f)^{-1}w_Y$ for $f\in W$. For resolutions $r$ over $R(X)$ and $s$ over $R(Y)$ the computed map is $\chi_sD(f)\chi_r^{-1}$, and its composite with $\chi_rw_X$ is $\chi_sw_YB(f)$. All these formulas use only the specified natural transformation $\tau$ and given resolution arrows. No inverse of $\tau_{R(X)}$ or $Q'G(r)$ and no lift of $a_X$ to $H$ is assumed.

proof.text: Write $F=L\circ Q$ and $T=Q'\circ G$, and write composition right to left, as in the statement. For a given $r:H\to R(X)$, $Q(r)$ is invertible because $Q$ localizes at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Functors preserve inverses, so $F(r)$ is invertible. Also $\tau_H$ is invertible by $H\in\mathcal P$. Consequently $\chi_r=\tau_HF(r)^{-1}$ has inverse $F(r)\tau_H^{-1}$: both products cancel to identities. The same argument applies to every specified resolution; it does not assert that resolutions exist for all objects.

source.place: Augmented-arrow calculus supplying the completed-pullback comparison; agent calculation

proof.text: Naturality of $\tau$ at $r$ gives $T(r)\tau_H=\tau_{R(X)}F(r)$, whence $T(r)\chi_r=\tau_{R(X)}$. Naturality at $a_X$ gives $\tau_{R(X)}F(a_X)=T(a_X)\tau_{S(X)}$. Since $S(X)\in\mathcal P$, postcomposing this equality with $\tau_{S(X)}^{-1}$ gives $\tau_{R(X)}w_X=T(a_X)$. Combining the two equalities yields $T(r)\chi_rw_X=T(a_X)$. This argument only inverts $F(r)$ and $\tau$ at good objects; it never inverts $T(r)$ or $\tau_{R(X)}$.

source.place: Augmented-arrow calculus supplying the completed-pullback comparison; agent calculation

proof.text: For resolutions $r,s,t$ of the same $R(X)$, insert $c_{s,r}=\chi_s\chi_r^{-1}$. Then $c_{s,r}\chi_rw_X=\chi_sw_X$ by $\chi_r^{-1}\chi_r=1$. Likewise $c_{t,s}c_{s,r}=\chi_t\chi_s^{-1}\chi_s\chi_r^{-1}=\chi_t\chi_r^{-1}=c_{t,r}$, and $c_{r,r}=\chi_r\chi_r^{-1}=1$. Thus the comparison and cocycle are defined even if no comparison arrow between resolutions is supplied.

source.place: Augmented-arrow calculus supplying the completed-pullback comparison; agent calculation

proof.text: Suppose $s:H'\to R(X)$ and $h:H\to H'$ satisfy $sh=r$. Naturality gives $T(h)\tau_H=\tau_{H'}F(h)$, and functoriality gives $F(s)F(h)=F(r)$. Multiplying by the already existing inverses implies $F(h)F(r)^{-1}=F(s)^{-1}$. Hence $T(h)\chi_r=\tau_{H'}F(h)F(r)^{-1}=\tau_{H'}F(s)^{-1}=\chi_s$. Postcompose with $\chi_r^{-1}$ to obtain $T(h)=c_{s,r}$. This is conditional on a given $h$; it is no lifting or existence assertion.

source.place: Augmented-arrow calculus supplying the completed-pullback comparison; agent calculation

proof.text:
Define the functors $B=T\circ S$ and $D=F\circ R$. For $f:X\to Y$, naturality of $a$ is $R(f)a_X=a_YS(f)$. Naturality of $\tau$ at $S(f)$, and invertibility at $S(X),S(Y)$, give $F(S(f))\tau_{S(X)}^{-1}=\tau_{S(Y)}^{-1}T(S(f))$. Therefore
$$D(f)w_X=F(R(f))F(a_X)\tau_{S(X)}^{-1}=F(a_Y)F(S(f))\tau_{S(X)}^{-1}=F(a_Y)\tau_{S(Y)}^{-1}T(S(f))=w_YB(f).$$
The components $w_X$ thus form a natural transformation $w:B\to D$.

source.place: Augmented-arrow calculus supplying the completed-pullback comparison; agent calculation

proof.text: Suppose $B$ and $D$ invert $W$. Apply clauses (1) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to the localization $q:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X[W^{-1}]$, target $D(\mathcal B)$, and the functors $B,D$ and transformation $w$ from Step 5. These clauses give lifts $\bar B,\bar D$, factorization isomorphisms $\phi_B:\bar Bq\simeq B$, $\phi_D:\bar Dq\simeq D$, and the unique descended transformation with component $\phi_{D,X}^{-1}w_X\phi_{B,X}$ at $qX$. This is descent with the usual factorization identifications, requiring no calculus of fractions for $W$. For $f\in W$, precompose $D(f)w_X=w_YB(f)$ with $D(f)^{-1}$ and postcompose with $B(f)^{-1}$ to get $w_XB(f)^{-1}=D(f)^{-1}w_Y$.

source.place: Tag 04VG, lemma-properties-left-localization, part (3); natural-transformation lifting as stated in the cited Mathlib leaf (Localization.liftNatTrans, liftNatTrans_app)

proof.text:
For $r:H\to R(X)$ and $s:H'\to R(Y)$ set $d_{s,r}(f)=\chi_sD(f)\chi_r^{-1}:T(H)\to T(H')$. This is $D(f)$ expressed through the two specified isomorphisms, so it is the computed map. Using Step 5,
$$d_{s,r}(f)\chi_rw_X=\chi_sD(f)w_X=\chi_sw_YB(f).$$
For completeness these coordinates respect composition: for a resolution $t$ over $R(Z)$ and $g:Y\to Z$,
$$d_{t,s}(g)d_{s,r}(f)=\chi_tD(g)\chi_s^{-1}\chi_sD(f)\chi_r^{-1}=\chi_tD(gf)\chi_r^{-1}=d_{t,r}(gf).$$
Every formula uses only $\tau$, the given arrows, their functorial images, and the inverses justified in Step 1. In particular the augmentation was never lifted to any $H$.
